title: Plymouth Barracuda Engines by Year (1964–1974)
description: Every factory engine in the Plymouth Barracuda and 'Cuda by year, 1964–1974: slant sixes, the Commando 273, 340, 383, 440 and 426 Hemi.
intro: Plymouth built the Barracuda for eleven model years, starting as a fastback Valiant in 1964 and ending as the E-body 'Cuda in 1974.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Barracuda used the Valiant's slant sixes and the 273 V8, with the four-barrel Commando 273 from 1965.

The 1967 redesign made room for the 383 big block. The 340 arrived in 1968, and a 'Cuda package added the 440 partway through 1969. Hurst built a small run of Hemi Barracudas for Super Stock racing in 1968.

The E-body Barracuda split its engines by model. The Barracuda and Gran Coupe ran from the slant six to the 383; the 'Cuda started at the 383 four-barrel and offered the 440 and 426 Hemi. The 1970 AAR 'Cuda had its own 340 with three two-barrel carburetors.
Ratings are advertised gross for 1970–1971 and SAE net from 1972, after the big blocks were gone.

excluded.name: 170 slant six

sources.name: Wikipedia: Plymouth Barracuda

excluded.researchNote: NHRA lists 170/101 (C-170-05). Not in the U.S. 1965 Barracuda brochure (225 is the 'Standard 6-cyl. Engine' and the only six) or Hagerty's 1965 configurations. Wikipedia (uncited) says the 170 stayed base only in Canada. Searched brochures, Hagerty, Old Cars Weekly, conceptcarz. Treat as Canada-market only; do not list for the U.S. car.

excluded.name: 198 slant six

sources.name: Wikipedia: Plymouth Barracuda

excluded.researchNote: Not in the 1970 Barracuda brochure spec table (225 is the only six, std on Barracuda/Gran Coupe) and not in NHRA 1970. The 1971 brochure introduces the 198 as std on the Barracuda Coupe. Treat as 1971-on; do not list for 1970.

excluded.name: 360 V8

sources.name: Wikipedia: Plymouth Barracuda

excluded.researchNote: Not in the 1973 brochure or in NHRA 1973. A search excerpt from a secondary site also says the 360 arrived mid-1973, but I could not find a second reputable source. Do not list for 1973.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
